info.title: RICADO Gen 3 REST API
info.description:
The RICADO Gen 3 REST API gives programmatic access to the sites, points, alarms, reports and configuration available in the RICADO Gen 3 web application. Requests act as the user whose credentials they carry, with that user's permissions.

Send credentials in the `Authorization` header: `Token <apiKey>:<apiSecret>` for integrations, or `Session <sessionId>` after a person signs in. These are RICADO schemes, not OAuth bearer tokens.

Each operation states its request format: form fields, raw JSON, or a JSON document inside a form field. Responses are JSON unless an operation says otherwise.

post.description:
**Important:**
- The whole batch is validated before anything is inserted. An invalid item, or a contactGroupId that is not an existing contact group on the site, rejects the entire request with HTTP 400 and item-indexed errors; no trigger is created.
- Accepted triggers are inserted in one transaction. On a caught failure the API attempts a rollback and returns HTTP 500. No partial success is reported, and the rollback's success is neither guaranteed nor reported.
- Send a JSON array of 1-500 items. For compatibility the API also accepts a JSON object whose keys are all non-negative integers, such as {"0": {...}}; its keys become the item indexes. Any other object root is rejected.

Authorization: Configurator site permission or higher (PERM_CONFIGURATOR).

triggerId.description: ID of the created RealComm trigger.

400.description: Bad request. Container errors (empty or invalid JSON, not an array, fewer than 1 or more than 500 items) use the shared errorMessage body. Item errors use an operation-specific body listing every invalid item, and reject the whole batch.

405.description: Method not allowed. No response body.

500.description: Server error. A failure inside the insert transaction returns this operation-specific body after a rollback attempt; no partial success is reported, and the rollback's success is not guaranteed or reported. Failures outside that transaction use the shared errorMessage body.

errorMessage.description: "An Unexpected Server Error Occurred", unless GEN3_ENVIRONMENT is development or testing, when the exception message is returned.

index.description: The item being inserted when the failure occurred; null if it happened before the first insert, for example while starting the transaction.

rtuSyncNodeId.description: RTU sync node ID: a positive, integer-valued number. The API accepts any numeric value equal to a whole number of at least 1, so a numeric string such as "12" is accepted; send a JSON integer. Fractional values (1.5, "1.5"), zero and negative values are rejected. Some forms the API also accepts are not expressed by this schema: 12.0, "12.0", "1.2e1" and a leading space (" 12").

contactGroupId.description: RealComm contact group ID, with the same positive integer-valued rules as rtuSyncNodeId (numeric strings accepted; fractional values rejected). It must also be an existing, non-deleted contact group on this site; otherwise the whole batch is rejected with HTTP 400.

name.description: Trigger name: a nonempty scalar of at most 255 characters after conversion to a string (counted as UTF-8 characters). Send a string. Numbers and true are scalars too and are stored as text; empty values ("", "0", 0 and false) and non-scalar values are rejected.

enabled.description: Required. The API compares strictly and accepts exactly true, false, 1, 0, "true", "false", "1" or "0". Everything else is rejected, including null, uppercase strings such as "TRUE", other numbers, and floating-point forms such as 1.0. A JSON Schema validator may treat 1.0 as equal to 1, but the API rejects it.

setDelay.description: Optional. A numeric value of at least 1000 is converted to an integer and stored. Any other value (missing, non-numeric or below 1000) is ignored without an error, and the default 1000 is used. The source does not state the unit.

resetDelay.description: Optional; the same rules as setDelay. Values that are non-numeric or below 1000 are ignored and the default 1000 is used.

serviceModePointId.description: Optional service-mode point ID. A nonempty numeric value is converted to an integer and stored; any other value is ignored without an error.

conditions.description: Trigger conditions as a nonempty scalar, stored as a string. When present and nonempty it takes precedence, and setConditions and resetConditions are then ignored, not validated. Required unless both setConditions and resetConditions are supplied; an empty value counts as absent.

setConditions.description: Set conditions, used only when conditions is absent or empty; then setConditions and resetConditions are both required as nonempty scalars and stored as strings. Supplying them alongside a nonempty conditions is not rejected: they are ignored.

resetConditions.description: Reset conditions, used only when conditions is absent or empty; see setConditions.

smsMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

callMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

emailMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

setTemplate.description: Messages used when the trigger sets. At least one of setTemplate or resetTemplate must be a nonempty object; both are allowed. A supplied template must contain nonempty scalar smsMessage, callMessage and emailMessage values.

smsMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

callMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

emailMessage.description: Must be a non-empty string; `""`, `"0"`, `0` and `false` count as empty.

resetTemplate.description: Messages used when the trigger resets. See setTemplate: at least one of the two templates is required.

items.description: Each item needs rtuSyncNodeId, contactGroupId, name and enabled. It also needs either a nonempty conditions, or both nonempty setConditions and resetConditions; and at least one nonempty setTemplate or resetTemplate (both are allowed). Empty values count as missing. Unrecognised keys are ignored.

schema.description: Canonical body: a raw JSON array (not a form field) of 1-500 trigger definitions. An empty body, invalid JSON, or an array with fewer than 1 or more than 500 items is rejected with the shared HTTP 400 errorMessage body. Compatibility quirk: a JSON object whose decoded keys are all non-negative integers (for example {"0": {...}, "1": {...}}) is iterated like an array, and its keys become the item indexes; any other object root is rejected. JSON Schema cannot describe that object form, so it is documented here only.
